body:
<!-- samuel:brief -->
> **What:** `/samuel:coordinate` (and `/samuel:cascade`, which reuses its dispatch protocol) launches Claude workers in an Orca terminal with the brief as the initial `claude` argument, and supervises them with `SendMessage` + `notify_when_idle` and a report file, instead of Orca dispatch, `check --wait` windows and lost-Enter checks.
> **Why:** Orca coordination cost 9.8% of context tokens (~$1,083 Opus) in the 30 days to 2026-10-02, with 550 blocking waits (12.9 h) and 475 relay prompts typed by the owner. Spike #63 confirmed the native path works inside Orca terminals.
> **Caveat:** The report file stays out of commits by instruction only, except in repos that gitignore `.claude/`. Codex workers keep the Orca path and its nag (#67).
> `L` · `risk medium` · `~1 day`

## Brief

**Scope:** the Claude-worker lane of `coordinate` (hub, `dispatch-protocol.md`, `worker-brief.md`), the shared references that describe it (`cross-session.md`, `orca-substrate.md`), the stale bare-name claim wherever it appears in `plugins/samuel` (including `conductor/SKILL.md` and `wave-protocol.md:172`), and the owner's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` section "When working with Orca".
**Out of scope:** the `waves` claude-variant completion signal (split to its own issue, blocked by this one); Codex/OpenCode supervision (#67); moving workers into in-session subagents; measuring the result (#72).

### Acceptance Criteria
- [x] AC1: A `/samuel:coordinate` run with one Claude writer worker completes with zero `orca orchestration task-create`, `worker-start`, `dispatch`, `--inject`, `terminal send … --enter` and `check --wait` calls for that worker (count them in the coordinator transcript).
- [x] AC2: The worker pane is visible in Orca, and a line the owner types into it is answered by the worker.
- [x] AC3: The coordinator ends at least one turn while the worker runs and resumes on the idle notice with no owner input and no `You have N orchestration messages` prompt.
- [x] AC4: The worker's six-line report is read from `{worktree}/.claude/reports/{name}.md`; the report file is not committed on the worker's branch.
- [x] AC5: `grep -rn 'bare name fails\|bare form fails\|the bare name is rejected' plugins/samuel` prints nothing; `reference/cross-session.md` carries the dated measurement from #63.
- [x] AC6: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` "When working with Orca" applies to Codex/OpenCode workers only, adds the Claude-worker rule in first person, and a dated backup exists.
- [x] AC7: Codex-worker instructions in `coordinate` and `cascade` are unchanged in behaviour (diff review); gates pass.

**Type:** feat  ·  **Priority:** high
**Depends on:** #63 (closed by its results comment). Blocks: the waves completion issue.

<!-- samuel:plan -->
## Executor Plan
> Self-contained. Assumes zero prior context. Written for an autonomous executor.

### Context
`plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate` is a coordinator skill: one session (the owner's flagship model) splits a task into briefed workers that run in Orca terminals, reads their reports, integrates and verifies. Today Claude and Codex workers share one path: `orca orchestration run-create` → `task-create` (brief as spec) → `worker-start` (Orca types the brief into the TUI) → prove the start within 30 s (lost-Enter check) → foreground `check --wait` windows of 9 min → `worker_done` mail carrying a six-line report → `worker-release`. Ending the coordinator turn with a dispatch open makes Orca type `You have N orchestration messages` into the owner's stream.

Spike #63 (results comment on that issue, Claude Code 2.1.288, Orca 1.4.218) measured inside Orca terminals:
- (a) `SendMessage` to a bare session name (`claude --name X`) delivers with no `[ref]`, no inbound setting, no approval dialog.
- (b) `SendMessage({to, notify_when_idle: true})` (with or without a message) yields exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` per subscription, carrying the worker's last line; a notice that fires while the coordinator is mid-turn is delivered at its next turn boundary; an exit produces one notice worded "is idle now".
- (c) `claude --name X --model M "$(cat brief.md)"` starts working with no Enter, 5/5; quotes, `$` and backticks arrive byte-exact.
- (e) the `Monitor` tool wakes an idle session on its next stdout line.
- (f) Orca's nag fires once per orchestration message that arrives, even when acked within 15 s, and is typed without Enter. A Claude worker with no Dispatch sends no orchestration messages, so it causes no nag.

`/samuel:cascade` has no launch mechanics of its own: `plugins/samuel/skills/cascade/SKILL.md:19` sends Orca workers to `../coordinate/references/dispatch-protocol.md` and `worker-brief.md`, so this change reaches cascade's Orca transport through those two files.

### Relevant code
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/SKILL.md:4` — `allowed-tools`; has no `SendMessage`, `ListAgents` or `Monitor`.
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/SKILL.md:53` — step 5 LAUNCH AND PROVE THE START (task-create, worker-start, receipt check, lost-Enter nudge).
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/SKILL.md:54` — step 6 SUPERVISE (foreground `check --wait`, "never end the turn while a dispatch is open").
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/SKILL.md:66-103` — Gotchas; lines 68, 69, 70, 92, 95, 98 describe the dispatch/lost-Enter/check-wait/heartbeat mechanism.
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/references/dispatch-protocol.md:66-120` — C3 launch: writer/reader `worker-start` lines (:71-77, :87-88), receipt check (:93-102), prove the start (:106-120).
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/references/dispatch-protocol.md:122-141` — C4 supervise (`check --wait` :127, liveness ladder :133-137, nag rule :141).
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/references/dispatch-protocol.md:143-157` — C5 reads the `worker_done` body; `worker-release`.
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/references/dispatch-protocol.md:177-185` — Recovery reads Run/Task/Dispatch state.
- `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/references/worker-brief.md:35-67` — six-slot brief; :54 the `worker_done` send; :78-89 report contract.
- `plugins/samuel/reference/cross-session.md:42`, `:129` — "a peer session is addressed with the ref, not the bare name" (stale per #63 a); `:99-107` "Where this is wired" (no coordinate); `:116`/`:136` "never gate an outcome on an inbox" (predates `notify_when_idle`).
- `plugins/samuel/skills/conductor/SKILL.md:67` — same stale bare-name claim.
- `plugins/samuel/skills/waves/references/wave-protocol.md:172` — same stale bare-name claim (only this line changes here; the waves lane is the split issue).
- `plugins/samuel/reference/orca-substrate.md:30-40` — worker lifecycle described as dispatch-only.
- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` § "When working with Orca (aug 2026)" (lines ~55-63) — lost-Enter rule for every worker launch, all engines.

### Approach
Split `coordinate`'s worker lane by engine. **Claude workers** (writers and readers): no Task, no Dispatch. The coordinator still binds an Orca Run (`run-create`/`run-use`) because the run policy is keyed by its id (`worker-brief.md:5-7`), but Claude workers never send orchestration messages, so the Run does not nag. **Codex workers** keep the current path unchanged.

Claude-worker lane:
1. **Brief file.** Write the filled brief (six slots + run policy appended, unchanged content) to `.claude/briefs/{run_id}/{name}.md` in the coordinator's checkout. The contract slots `REPORT` and the lifecycle preamble change: instead of `orca orchestration send --type worker_done`, the worker writes the six report lines to `.claude/reports/{name}.md` in its own worktree, never stages or commits that file, and ends its turn with the single line `REPORT .claude/reports/{name}.md`. Questions for the coordinator: the worker stops and ends its turn with `QUESTION: …` as its last line.
2. **Launch.** Writer: `orca worktree create --name {name} --repo id:{ORCA_REPO_ID} --setup run --json` (same naming and card rules as today), then `orca terminal create --worktree name:{name} --title {name} --command 'claude --name {name} --model {model} --effort {effort} --permission-mode auto "$(cat {abs brief path})"' --json`. Reader: the same `terminal create` with `--worktree current`. Interactive (no `-p`), so the owner can read and type in the pane. Link the card as today (`orca worktree set --issue`).
3. **Verify the launch.** Within 30 s, `orca terminal read --terminal {handle} --json`: the footer names the requested model and the brief is rendered as a sent `❯` message followed by a tool call. Wrong model ⇒ stop and tell the human. Effort cannot be read from the TUI; record it as "requested, not observable". A bare shell prompt with no TUI ⇒ dead agent: close the terminal and relaunch the same command once. No lost-Enter step: a brief passed as argv cannot sit in the input box.
4. **Supervise.** Right after the start is proven: `SendMessage({to: "{name}", notify_when_idle: true})` (no message; bare name — add the `[ref]` only when `ListAgents` shows two rows with that name). Arm one `Monitor` that prints a liveness tick every 9 minutes (e.g. `while true; do sleep 540; echo tick; done`, timeout 30 min, re-armed on expiry). The coordinator **may end its turn** while only Claude workers are open. On each idle notice: if the last line is `REPORT …`, go to C5; if it is `QUESTION: …`, answer with `SendMessage` (scope/schema/other workers' files go to the human first) and re-subscribe; otherwise it is an early stop — send one continue message that names the open items from the brief's DELIVER/VERIFY and asks what blocks any of them, re-subscribe, at most 2 per worker, then escalate to the human. On a Monitor tick with no notice: `orca terminal read` (permission prompt ⇒ stop that worker, fix the launch, relaunch; never answer it from the coordinator) and `git log --oneline -3 {branch}`; one status line per worker. Quota death detection is unchanged (dirty tree, no commits, a usage-limit line).
5. **Read and release.** C5 reads `{worktree}/.claude/reports/{name}.md` instead of the `worker_done` body; the frozen-commit checks are unchanged. Release = `orca terminal close --terminal {handle}` (call twice if the first returns not-closed). Recovery after compaction: Claude workers are found with `ListAgents` plus `orca worktree ps`, and their briefs/reports are on disk.

Documentation follows the same split: shared references stop claiming the bare name fails and record `notify_when_idle` as the one allowed wait on an inbox (the notice is pushed by the harness, not polled).

### Testing seams
none — repo has no test suite

### Steps
1. **Split C3–C5 by engine** — `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/references/dispatch-protocol.md` — under C3 add a `### Claude workers — argv brief, no dispatch` subsection with Approach items 1–3 as exact commands; keep the existing `worker-start` lines only under a `### Codex workers` subsection (delete the Claude `worker-start` lines at :71-73 and :88). In C4 add `### Claude workers` with Approach item 4 and scope the `check --wait` loop, the liveness ladder and the "turn does not end while a dispatch is open" rule (:141) to Codex workers. In C5 add the report-file read and the terminal-close release for Claude workers. In Recovery add the `ListAgents` + `worktree ps` lookup.
   Verify: `grep -n 'agent claude' plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/references/dispatch-protocol.md` prints nothing; `grep -c 'notify_when_idle' …dispatch-protocol.md` ≥ 1.
2. **Report contract** — `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/references/worker-brief.md` — in the contract/preamble (:35-67) and report section (:78-89) add the Claude-worker form: write the six lines to `.claude/reports/{name}.md`, never stage it, last line `REPORT .claude/reports/{name}.md`, questions as a last line `QUESTION: …`; brief files live at `.claude/briefs/{run_id}/{name}.md`. Keep the `worker_done` form for Codex.
   Verify: both forms appear, each labelled with its engine.
3. **Hub** — `plugins/samuel/skills/coordinate/SKILL.md` — add `ListAgents SendMessage Monitor` to `allowed-tools` (:4). Rewrite steps 5 and 6 (:53-54) to name the two lanes in one sentence each and point to C3/C4. In Gotchas, label the dispatch-only items (:68, :69, :70, :92, :95, :98) as Codex-worker items in their own text; delete any that only described Claude workers. Add one gotcha: an idle notice that fires while the coordinator is mid-turn arrives at its next turn boundary, not immediately.
   Verify: `bash scripts/lint-skill-context.sh` passes (every binary the hub runs is declared).
4. **Cross-session reference** — `plugins/samuel/reference/cross-session.md` — replace the bare-name rule at :42 and the gotcha at :129 with: since Claude Code 2.1.288 (measured 2026-10-02, #63) a bare name delivers when it matches one live session; add the `[ref]` only when `ListAgents` shows two rows with that name. Add `coordinate` to "Where this is wired" (:99-107). Next to :116/:136, state that `notify_when_idle` is the exception to "never gate an outcome on an inbox": the harness pushes one notice per subscription; the outcome itself is still read from a durable record (the report file, the branch, the PR).
   Verify: AC5 grep prints nothing.
5. **Other stale claims** — `plugins/samuel/skills/conductor/SKILL.md:67` and `plugins/samuel/skills/waves/references/wave-protocol.md:172` — replace "a peer session takes `name [ref]`, and the bare name fails" with the rule from Step 4 (one sentence, point to `cross-session.md`). Change nothing else in waves.
   Verify: AC5 grep; `git diff --stat` shows one or two lines in each file.
6. **Substrate** — `plugins/samuel/reference/orca-substrate.md:30-40` — say the dispatch lifecycle is the Codex/OpenCode lane; Claude workers in `coordinate` use `terminal create` + argv brief + `SendMessage` (one line, point to C3).
   Verify: the lifecycle line names both lanes.
7. **Owner's global instructions** — `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` — first `cp ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d)`. Then scope "When working with Orca" to Codex and OpenCode workers and add, in first person, "I want Claude workers launched with the brief as the `claude` argument and supervised with `SendMessage` + `notify_when_idle`; the lost-Enter check is for Codex and OpenCode only." Write in first person: the auto-mode classifier blocks imperative edits to that file. If the edit is denied, put the exact proposed text in the PR body as a pending owner step.
   Verify: `diff ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.bak-* ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` shows only that section.
8. **Live run** — in an Orca terminal, run `/samuel:coordinate` on a throwaway S task (e.g. "add one line to docs/research/README.md" on a scratch branch) routed to one Claude writer (`--engine claude`). Count the forbidden calls (AC1), type one line into the worker pane (AC2), let the coordinator end its turn (AC3), check the report file is uncommitted (AC4). Close the worker and remove the scratch worktree afterwards.
   Verify: AC1–AC4 observed; paste the counts into the PR body.

### Guardrails
- English only in skills and references; keep the hub-and-spoke split (detail in `references/`, the hub points to it).
- Every binary a skill runs must be declared in its own `allowed-tools` — headless denial is silent (`scripts/lint-skill-context.sh` enforces it).
- Do not change Codex-worker commands, the `--via conductor` / `--via iaas` opt-ins, cascade's `--transport agents`, or the waves claude variant beyond Step 5's line.
- Comments and gotchas state constraints the text cannot show; no narration of the change.
- No push, PR, merge or GitHub write outside the run's authority; `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is edited only after the backup exists.

### Validation
- **Automated (gate):** `bun run check:context && bun run check:plugins && bun run check:portability && bun run check:autonomy`
- **Manual:** Step 8. Given Orca is up and the coordinator runs in an Orca terminal, When `/samuel:coordinate` routes one S task to a Claude writer, Then the worker starts with no Enter, the coordinator ends a turn, one idle notice resumes it, the report is read from `.claude/reports/{name}.md`, and no `You have N orchestration messages` appears.

### Definition of Done
- [x] All Steps complete
- [x] Gate green
- [ ] Every Brief AC met, with Step 8's counts in the PR body
- [x] `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` backup present (or the proposed text listed as a pending owner step)
title: feat(coordinate): Claude workers start with the brief as argument and are supervised with SendMessage
